audience: people living paycheck to paycheck who open the banking app and still don't know what is really theirs to spend
freelancers, tipped, gig and commission workers whose pay lands on different days in different amounts
people who have started and dropped a budget (or YNAB, or a 12-tab spreadsheet) more than once and are tired of catching up
beginners who search 'budgeting for beginners' and save one-page budget sheets and weekly money check-in lists
savers building a first $1,000 emergency fund, and people who save cash-envelope and savings-tracker pins
anyone resetting at the end of the month or before holiday spending, who wants to start clean from today's balance

visualWorld.setting: A kitchen table and fridge door on a Sunday evening, seen flat-lay from above or straight on: the paper side of month-to-month money. Kraft envelopes holding bill money back, a wall calendar with bill stickers and paydays, a torn till receipt that shows the working, a price tag on a coffee cup, a jar on the counter, a one-page printout under a fridge magnet. One month at a time, always paper, never a bank dashboard (that is Personal Finance Companion's world: accounts, debt payoff curves, statement imports, subscriptions lists across cards).

props.draw: A deep forest rounded rectangle (the 'Number' panel) with a dark slot line cut across its lower edge; a tall off-white till receipt hangs from the slot. Receipt: straight top edge, zigzag torn bottom (12px teeth), faint drop shadow, rows of label + dotted leader + right-aligned mono figure, a sign column (+ in sage-green, minus in muted grey), a double rule above the bold total line. Mirrors SafeToSpendCard.tsx.

Kraft envelopes (rectangle plus a flap drawn as a downward triangle with a 3px darker edge), each with a white label window (rounded rectangle) holding a name, an amount and a due date. Sealed variant: a clay paper band wrapped round the middle. Open variant: flap up, a slip of paper with a figure poking out. No banknotes, no coins: the envelope stands for money held back, not a cash system.

A wall-calendar page hanging from a black binder clip: header strip with the month name, 7 columns x 5 rows of squares with small date numerals top-left; bill stickers are clay rounded tabs with a name and amount; paydays are sage tabs; one date ringed by a hand-drawn clay circle (an open ellipse with a slight overlap).

A thin step line running under the calendar, one step per dated bill or payday, dropping at bills and rising at pay; the lowest step gets a filled clay dot and a pill chip reading 'Tightest' + date + mono amount, the same chip shape the product shows.

A short wide slip with a perforated left edge (row of small circles), a name line and a mono amount. 'Received' version: solid outline and a small sage check. 'Expected' version: dashed outline, 60% opacity, a small grey stamp-box reading 'not counted yet'.
A takeaway cup: tapered trapezoid body, a lid as a flat rounded band, a kraft sleeve band round the middle; a swing tag on a curved string hangs from the lid.
A kraft tag: rectangle with two clipped top corners, a punched hole (circle) with a looped string; large mono price; optional verdict written underneath in small sans.
A flat paper grocery bag: rectangle with a zigzag top edge and a folded side gusset line, one leafy shape (three ellipses) poking out.

A mason jar: rounded body, a lid of two horizontal bands, a measuring scale of short ticks on one side with labels up to $1,000, the fill drawn as stacked horizontal colour bands (each band a deposit), a couple of coins (circles with an inner ring) dropping in from above.

The full canvas as a fridge door: soft warm-white panel, one long vertical handle (rounded bar) at the left edge, a faint seam line near the top. Holds paper with round and square magnets (flat circles with a highlight crescent).

A sheet of paper rotated -2 degrees with a thin header rule, small caps section labels, rows with dotted leaders and right-aligned figures, or square tick boxes with ticks drawn as two-stroke check marks.
A ruled index card: rectangle with one red-clay top rule and pale blue-grey lines, square tick boxes at the left of each line.
A round kitchen timer: circle with a smaller dial circle, tick marks round the edge, a pointer at the minute mark the pin names, a small knob on top.
A square note with a slightly curled bottom-right corner (a small triangle in a darker tint), held by one magnet.
Two calendar or ledger pages side by side: the left one greyed and curling at one corner, the right one crisp; a bold clay arrow between them.
A shoebox (open box drawn as a parallelogram rim and front face) overflowing with curled grey receipt strips; drawn at low contrast, the thing you no longer need to sort.
A thick ring binder seen from the side with twelve coloured index tabs sticking out, slightly bulging; drawn heavy, the 'whole system' in a contrast pin.
A row with a label and a pill toggle (rounded track, circle knob at the right when on, forest-filled).

A rounded phone frame (390-wide aspect) holding the real capture creative/public/screens/monthly-money-reset-progress.png, cropped to its top cards or its footer line; never a re-drawn or invented screen.
A short pencil: hexagonal body as a long rectangle, a cone tip, a clay ferrule band and eraser.

visualWorld.palette: The product's own tokens from src/products/monthly-money-reset/theme.ts: forest #173c32 (hero panels, headline ink on light grounds), sage #96a58f / sage-soft #dce2d7 / sage-pale #edf0e9 (paydays, received income, calm fills), ivory #f5f0e8 and paper #fffdf9 (table, receipts, sheets), ink #18231f, line #ded8cd. Clay #b86f4a and clay-soft #f2e2d8 are the single warm accent: envelope bands, bill stickers, the tightest-day ring, price tags. Kraft is clay-soft deepened toward line #cbc3b7, not a new hue. No alarm red; a negative number would use the product's own danger #9e4f44 sparingly.
visualWorld.mood: Calm and practical: a quiet Sunday sort-out at the kitchen table, not a hustle or a no-spend dare. Honest paper, real figures with their working shown, nothing scored or streaked. The tone of the product itself: 'It shows you the picture; the decisions stay yours.'

archetypes.name: The receipt
archetypes.clicks: Money pins that show a specific figure and the arithmetic behind it are the niche's staple: benefit-led, number-forward headlines are recommended over generic labels (Tailwind), and finance pins that promise a specific outcome or number are the advice from finance bloggers (businessjournalism.org). A receipt reads instantly as 'here is the math' and is saved as a reference for doing your own sum. It is also this product's real signature: the Number panel with a torn receipt hanging from it (SafeToSpendCard.tsx).
archetypes.layout: 1000x1500 on ivory. Small Draftpace logo top-left (40px, never bottom-right). Headline y 90-430, left-aligned at x 70, forest ink, bold sans, 2-3 lines, max ~64px. Forest Number panel y 470-660 spanning x 70-930 with a small-caps label (e.g. 'SAFE TO SPEND NOW') and the big total in mono. The receipt hangs from the panel's slot, x 180-820, y 640-1260, torn bottom edge; 4-7 rows of label, dotted leader, mono figure; double rule; bold total. Sub line y 1290-1350 at x 70. Product line (name, free/price) bottom-left y 1390-1450; keep x>800, y>1350 empty.
archetypes.visual: The forest panel, the hanging receipt with its working, optionally a paycheck stub or keypad clipped beside it.
archetypes.text: Headline; panel label and total; receipt lines copied from the product's real labels (SafeToSpendCard.tsx / PrintablesModule.tsx BREAKDOWN_LINES) with figures from DEMO_STATE or a guide's worked example, labelled 'Example'; one real sub line.
archetypes.bestFor: safe to spend, one-page budget, restart from today, check-in result, no bank linking, savings taken off first

archetypes.name: Held-back envelopes
archetypes.clicks: Cash-envelope and cash-stuffing flat-lays are one of the most recognisable money aesthetics online: cash stuffing passed 700 million TikTok views (Tom's Guide) and Pinterest reported envelope-challenge searches up 145% in its 2023 predictions coverage. The audience stops on labelled envelopes. Here the envelopes hold back named bills and reserves, which is exactly what 'protected' means in the product, without claiming a cash system.
archetypes.layout: Top-down flat-lay on an ivory table. Logo top-left. Headline y 80-420. Envelopes fan diagonally across y 500-1220, 3-5 of them, largest at front, each label window legible (name / mono amount / due date). Sealed ones carry a clay band; one open envelope at front-left with a slip showing what is left. A small 'Money available right now' slip or paycheck stub can sit top-right of the fan. Sub y 1270-1340. Product line bottom-left; bottom-right clear.
archetypes.visual: Kraft envelopes with label windows, clay bands, one open envelope with a figure slip, optionally a paycheck stub or coffee cup tucked in.
archetypes.text: Envelope labels are real bill/reserve/group names and amounts from DEMO_STATE or real labels from the product (Essentials / Flexible / Personal, 'Carries over' rows from the guide table); headline and one sub line.
archetypes.bestFor: protect bills, reserve and savings held back first, spending groups instead of 40 categories, what carries into next month

archetypes.name: Bill calendar with the tightest day
archetypes.clicks: Bill calendars and paycheck-budget printables are a standard format in the niche (budget-by-paycheck and bill-calendar templates are sold and pinned widely), because a date is concrete in a way an average is not. A ringed date with an amount is a single, mobile-readable idea (Pinterest's own advice: concise copy, product front and centre). It shows the product's most distinctive feature, the tightest day, which no generic budget pin shows.
archetypes.layout: Logo top-left. Headline y 80-400. Wall calendar hangs from a binder clip, x 90-910, y 440-1180: month header, 7x5 grid, clay bill tabs and sage payday tabs on their dates, one date ringed in clay. Balance line y 1190-1300 under the grid, its lowest step dotted with the 'Tightest' chip. Sub y 1320-1370. Product line bottom-left. Variant for week-by-week topics: replace the grid with 6-8 week rows.
archetypes.visual: Calendar page, bill and payday stickers, ringed day, balance step line, optional dashed 'expected' stub or a price tag pinned to a day.
archetypes.text: Month name, real bill names/amounts/dates from DEMO_STATE (or a guide's dated example, labelled), the chip 'Tightest' + date + amount as the product prints it (SafeToSpendCard.tsx), headline, sub.
archetypes.bestFor: tightest day, paycheck to paycheck, irregular income dates, bills due soon, starting again on day one, budgets that drift

archetypes.name: The price-tag test
archetypes.clicks: 'Can I afford this?' is how this audience actually searches (it is one of the product's sourced searchedProblems), and a relatable object with a price makes the pin instantly about them. A tag plus a before/after figure is a number-forward comparison, the benefit-led format Tailwind recommends, and it suits POV-style Maple pins.
archetypes.layout: Logo top-left. Headline as a question y 80-400. Hero object (coffee cup, grocery bag or a row of tags on a rail) left half x 70-480, y 470-1180, with a big kraft swing tag. Right half x 520-930: 2-4 narrow result tickets stacked (if you buy / left to spend / per week / verdict), mono figures. Sub y 1230-1320. Product line bottom-left.
archetypes.visual: Coffee cup, grocery bag or tag rail; kraft swing tags; stacked result tickets.
archetypes.text: Prices and results from a guide's worked table (can-you-afford-it-before-you-buy-it, how-to-find-every-subscription-you-are-paying-for) labelled 'Example', or the product mockup's '$600.00 to $558.00' line; verdict words copied from the guide.
archetypes.bestFor: can I afford it, overspending, impulse buys, subscriptions' yearly cost, mental math at the checkout, ways to save this month

archetypes.name: On the fridge
archetypes.clicks: Checklists and printable sheets are the niche's most-saved reference format: budget-checklist pin templates, savings trackers and budget binders are sold and pinned in bulk, and people save them to come back to. Pinterest's guidance favours one clear idea readable on a phone. A sheet under a fridge magnet says 'routine' and 'keep this', and the product really does make a one-page PDF meant for the fridge (wave4 pin 8.2: 'Stick it on the fridge').
archetypes.layout: Canvas is the fridge door; handle bar down the left edge. Logo top-left inside the door. Headline y 70-360 as large type on the door. Sheet x 140-880, y 400-1260, rotated -2 degrees, held by 2 magnets; 3-6 tick-box rows or the PDF snapshot's sections. Optional: a kitchen timer magnet top-right of the sheet, a sticky note, or a phone with the real Progress screenshot leaning bottom-left (x 70-380, y 1050-1400) in place of the sub. Sub y 1290-1350. Product line bottom-left.
archetypes.visual: Fridge door, printed sheet or index card with tick boxes, magnets, timer, sticky note, optional phone with the real screenshot.
archetypes.text: Check-in questions from CheckInModal.tsx QUESTIONS, step lists copied from the pin's own description or its guide, or the PDF section labels from printables/generatePdf.tsx with DEMO_STATE figures.
archetypes.bestFor: weekly check-in, step lists, end-of-month review, the one-page PDF, picking it back up after a missed week, cancellation note

archetypes.name: Turn the page
archetypes.clicks: Fresh-start and reset content is a seasonal driver (month end, New Year, before the holidays) and the 'reset' framing is how this product is named. A two-page before/after is the simplest visual story Pinterest users read at a glance: what you leave behind, what you keep. It answers the restart fear ('do I have to catch up?') with a picture rather than a claim.
archetypes.layout: Logo top-left. Headline y 80-400. Two sheets on the table y 460-1200: left x 60-470 greyed and curling (old month, receipt pile or a 12-tab binder), right x 530-940 crisp (new month with toggle rows or the starting-balance choices); clay arrow between at y ~830. Three-step variant: three cards stepping diagonally down-right with numbered circles. Sub y 1250-1320. Product line bottom-left.
archetypes.visual: Month pages, receipt pile or tab binder on the left, carry-forward toggles or starting-balance chips on the right, a clay arrow; optional phone with the real Progress screenshot as the right page.
archetypes.text: Carry-forward labels and starting-balance options from HistoryModule.tsx (Recurring income, Recurring bills, Spending groups, Reserve preference, Check-in preference; Suggested, Actual balance, Custom amount, Start fresh), Setup step titles from SetupModule.tsx STEPS, or step words from the pin's own description.
archetypes.bestFor: close the month, monthly reset, restart after falling off, one page vs a whole system, three-step how-tos

archetypes.name: The jar
archetypes.clicks: Savings trackers to colour in (jars, thermometers, 52-week and bi-weekly charts) are among the most pinned money printables; Pinterest reported bi-weekly savings challenge searches more than tripled (Pinterest Predicts 2023 coverage). '$1,000' is a specific, reachable goal, the outcome-led number finance pins are advised to lead with. Used only where the guide supplies the numbers, since the product holds a reserve back but does not track a savings goal.
archetypes.layout: Logo top-left. Headline y 80-380. Tall jar centred x 300-700, y 420-1220, tick scale on its right side to $1,000, fill bands per deposit; to the left x 60-280, the guide's table as tick labels (amount / how often / time). Coins dropping at the top. Irregular-income variant: six paycheck stubs of different heights feeding the jar labelled 'Holding account', one even stub leaving it. Tracker variant (no money amounts): four colour-in cells. Sub y 1260-1330. Product line bottom-left.
archetypes.visual: Mason jar with scale and fill bands, coins, paycheck stubs, or colour-in cells.
archetypes.text: Only a guide's own example numbers, labelled 'Example from the guide', or the pin's own words in the tracker variant.
archetypes.bestFor: first $1,000 emergency fund, irregular income holding account, small-wins tracker
